podcast.body: This song was part of a series of demos recorded by Jonathan Richman in 1971. It featured a stripped-down sound, characterized by droning fuzz and distortion, combined with sharp and pointed lyrics. Richman famously forbade guitar and drum solos, creating a sound very different from the mainstream rock of the era. The song is noted for sounding like something an indie band might release today and was considered a "harbinger for the punk to come," though the timing wasn't quite right for its widespread acceptance. "Jonathan Richmond and Roadrunner from 1971."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song features Jonathan Richman singing about blasting the radio in a Plymouth Roadrunner while driving on Route 128 in Massachusetts. There is an ongoing effort to designate it as the state's official rock song. "From 1972, that's Jonathan Richmond singing about blasting the radio in a Plymouth Roadrunner while tearing up Route 128 in Massachusetts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
